name: @monofile/mcp

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Run a shell command in your workspace. Read-only chains of pwd/ls/tree/cat/head/tail/stat/wc/find/grep run instantly against the database; anything else (pipes, sed/awk/sort/jq, redirects, git, python3, node, scripts) runs in a real sh with real coreutils inside a persistent per-workspace sandbox whose disk mirrors the workspace. Files the command creates, edits, renames or deletes are written back into the workspace (versioned, one changeset per call) and reported in `changes`; `conflicts` lists files that changed elsewhere while the command ran (your version won). Scopes are enforced on the write-back: creating/editing needs files:write, deleting needs files:delete — a missing scope rejects the whole diff (INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE) and nothing is written. Paths are workspace-absolute (/Projects/a.md). Optional: `timeout` seconds (default 60, max 240), `cwd`, `debug: true` for sandbox details; `timings` (ms) is always returned. Errors: SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE, SANDBOX_BUSY (one command per workspace at a time), RATE_LIMITED, SANDBOX_NOT_ENTITLED (the full shell is part of paid plans; built-in commands then run on the built-in shell), INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS, DIFF_TOO_LARGE, TIMEOUT (partial changes written back). Output is capped at 400 lines / 30 KB.

command.description: Unix-style command to execute. Examples: 'ls -la /Projects', 'grep -rin "TODO" /src', 'cat -n /file.txt', 'find /src -name "*.ts" -type f', 'tree --depth 2 /Projects'.

timeout.description: Real shell only: seconds before the command is killed (default 60, max 240 — larger values are clamped)

cwd.description: Real shell only: working directory, workspace-absolute without '..' segments (default /)

debug.description: Real shell only: include sandbox/usage details in the result

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file by path. Returns raw content with optional metadata.

path.description: The full path to the file (e.g., '/Projects/auth.py')

includeMetadata.description: Include file metadata (id, name, path, mimeType, language, size, lines, modified). Default: false

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create a new file or overwrite an existing file by path. Automatically creates parent folders if needed. For .draw diagram files use create_diagram (Mermaid in, editable diagram out) — never hand-write Excalidraw JSON.

path.description: The full path where the file should be created (e.g., '/Projects/Backend/auth.py')

content.description: The content to write to the file

createParents.description: Create parent folders if they don't exist. Default: true

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Make selective edits to a file using exact text matching. Provide old_string (text to find) and new_string (replacement). Pass expectedUpdatedAt (ISO timestamp from a prior read/stat) for optimistic concurrency — the edit fails with EDIT_CONFLICT if the file changed since.

path.description: The full path to the file (e.g., '/Projects/auth.py')

old_string.description: The exact text to find and replace (case-sensitive)

new_string.description: The replacement text (can be empty to delete the matched text)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences. If false (default), fails when >1 match found.

dryRun.description: Preview changes without applying them. Default: false

showDiff.description: Include unified diff in response. Default: true

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Expected last modified timestamp (ISO string). If provided and file was modified since, returns EDIT_CONFLICT error. Used for conflict detection in multi-agent scenarios.

tools.name: get_folder_share_status

folderId.description: The folder path (e.g., '/my-project') or unique ID of the folder to check

tools.name: share_folder
tools.description: Make a top-level folder and all its contents publicly accessible by creating a share link. Anyone with the link can view the folder and browse its files. Only root-level folders can be shared.

folderId.description: The folder path (e.g., '/my-project') or unique ID of the folder to share

tools.name: unshare_folder
tools.description: Revoke public sharing for a folder, making it and all its contents private again. The existing share URL will stop working.

folderId.description: The folder path (e.g., '/my-project') or unique ID of the folder to make private

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: Create (or update) a private share link for a FILE — a secret, revocable URL (/l/<token>) that anyone with the link can view, without a Monofile account. The file stays out of the community, feeds, search, and search engines. One link per file: if a link already exists this updates it with the given options and returns it (created: false) — it never fails with a conflict. freeze: true pins the CURRENT content (later edits won't change what viewers see); freeze: false returns the link to live-latest. password (min 6 chars) adds a password gate viewers must pass; password: null removes it; changing it signs every viewer out. Folders are not supported — use share_folder for public folder sharing.

path.description: Full path to the file (e.g., '/notes/plan.md'), or a file id

expiresInHours.description: Auto-expire the link after this many hours. Omit for no expiry.

freeze.description: true = pin the current content (later edits won't change what viewers see); false = follow latest content. Omit to leave pin state unchanged.

password.description: Set a password viewers must enter (6-72 chars); null removes it; omit to leave unchanged. Setting or changing it signs every current viewer out.

tools.name: get_share_link
tools.description: Check whether a file has a private share link. Returns exists: false if none, or the link's url, view count, expiry, and pin state. Read-only. For public folder shares use get_folder_share_status instead.

path.description: Full path to the file, or a file id

tools.name: revoke_share_link
tools.description: Revoke a file's private share link. The URL stops working immediately and permanently (creating a new link later generates a different URL). Errors with LINK_NOT_FOUND if the file has no link.

path.description: Full path to the file, or a file id

tools.name: create_canvas
tools.description:
Create a .canvas board (JSON Canvas) from a compact spec: nodes (text notes, file previews, links, groups) and edges between them, with optional auto-layout. HTML file nodes render LIVE as artboards at the node size (390×844 mobile, 1440×900 desktop); pass `content` on a file node to write the file in the same call. Edges may reference nodes as $1..$n (index into `nodes`) or $ref. Fails if the file exists unless overwrite: true.

A `.canvas` file is JSON Canvas 1.0 (https://jsoncanvas.org) plus an optional `x-monofile` object. Version: `1.0-mf1`.

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718",
      "type": "file",
      "file": "screens/home.html",
      "x": 0,
      "y": 0,
      "width": 390,
      "height": 844
    },
    {
      "id": "b2c3d4e5f6071829",
      "type": "file",
      "file": "notes/spec.md",
      "x": 480,
      "y": 0,
      "width": 420,
      "height": 300
    },
    {
      "id": "c3d4e5f607182930",
      "type": "text",
      "text": "## Open questions\n- pricing copy",
      "x": 480,
      "y": 360,
      "width": 260,
      "height": 140,
      "color": "3"
    },
    {
      "id": "d4e5f60718293041",
      "type": "group",
      "label": "Mobile v2",
      "x": -40,
      "y": -60,
      "width": 980,
      "height": 980
    }
  ],
  "edges": [
    {
      "id": "e5f6071829304152",
      "fromNode": "b2c3d4e5f6071829",
      "fromSide": "left",
      "toNode": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718",
      "toSide": "right",
      "label": "implements"
    }
  ],
  "x-monofile": {
    "version": "1.0-mf1"
  }
}
```

Rules:
- Node types: `text` (markdown in `text`), `file` (workspace-relative `file` path, no leading `/`), `link` (`url`), `group` (`label`). Never invent other types.
- `x`, `y` = top-left corner in px (x→right, y→down); `width`/`height` required integers. Array order = z-order (last on top).
- Sizes: text 260×140, file 420×300, link 320×120. HTML files render LIVE as artboards at the node size — use viewport presets: Mobile 390×844 · Tablet 820×1180 · Desktop 1440×900 · Slide 16:9 1280×720.
- Edges: `fromNode`/`toNode` ids, optional `fromSide`/`toSide` (top|right|bottom|left), `label`, `color`. Arrow at the `to` end by default.
- Colors: `"#RRGGBB"` or presets `"1"` red · `"2"` orange · `"3"` yellow · `"4"` green · `"5"` cyan · `"6"` purple.
- Ids: any unique string without `-` (Monofile mints 16 hex chars). Omit ids and the server assigns them.
- Max 500 nodes. Leave 60–120 px between nodes; group related nodes with a `group` that encloses them geometrically.
- Prefer the `canvas_edit` tool (batched ops, auto-layout) over hand-writing JSON; a plain `write` of valid JSON also works.

ref.description: Name this node so later ops can refer to it as $name

file.description: file nodes: workspace-relative path, e.g. screens/home.html

overwrite.description: with content: replace the file if it already exists (default: FILE_EXISTS error)

content.description: file nodes only: create/overwrite the referenced file with this content in the same call (e.g. the HTML of an artboard)

nodes.description: Nodes to add (same fields as the add_node op)

fromNode.description: A node/edge id, or a "$n" / "$name" reference to an earlier op in this batch

toNode.description: A node/edge id, or a "$n" / "$name" reference to an earlier op in this batch

edges.description: Edges to add; fromNode/toNode may be $n (1-based index into `nodes`) or $ref

layout.description: Auto-layout direction after adding (recommended when you omit x/y)

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file instead of failing (default false)

tools.name: canvas_check
tools.description: Check a .canvas board's file references and report what is broken, without reading raw JSON. Per file node it reports one of: ok, path_stale (the file moved, the node's portable path did not), path_only (no stable id — one rename from breaking), unresolved_id (an id from another workspace, e.g. a fork), missing (nothing matches), section_missing (the `#heading` is not in the file), subpath_ignored (a `#section` on a file that has no sections). Pass `repair: true` to rewrite the fixable ones (path_stale, path_only) in place. Read-only unless `repair` is set, which additionally requires `files:write`.

path.description: Full path to the .canvas file to check (e.g., '/boards/roadmap.canvas')

repair.description: Rewrite the fixable references (path_stale, path_only) in place. Default: false (read-only). Requires files:write.

tools.name: create_slides
tools.description:
Create a .slides deck (markdown slides, rendered as a presentation with speaker notes, presenter view and export) from structured slides: each `{ layout?, content?, notes?, src?, html?, id? }`. `content` is markdown by default, raw HTML with `html: true`, or a full HTML document; `src` shows an existing workspace file (.html artboard, .md, image) as the slide. Give every slide an `id` so later `slides_edit` calls can address it. Fails if the file exists unless overwrite: true. For free-form authoring, `write` works too — a deck is plain markdown. A `.slides` file is a markdown deck: an optional YAML headmatter, then slides separated by a line that is exactly `---`. ```markdown --- title: Q3 Review theme: midnight size: 16:9 --- # Q3 Review A quarter in three slides --- layout: two-column id: numbers --- ## Revenue - Up 32% quarter over quarter - Churn down to 1.1% ![[charts/revenue.png]] **Net: ahead of plan.** --- html: true background: "#0b0b0f" ---

Design, live.

Any HTML you write renders as a slide.

--- src: designs/hero.html --- --- layout: section skip: true --- # Appendix ``` Rules: - Headmatter keys: `title`, `theme` (default | midnight | paper | gradient), `size` (16:9 = 1280×720, 4:3 = 1024×768, 16:10 = 1280×800, or WxH), `author`, `paginate`, `style` (CSS appended to the theme). - A slide may open with its own `---`-closed YAML frontmatter right after the separator: `id` (stable handle, recommended), `layout`, `class`, `background` (color or image path), `html: true` (body is raw HTML), `src` (render a workspace file as the slide), `skip` (not numbered), `title`. - Layouts: default | title | section | two-column | image | quote | blank. Word budgets per layout (body, advisory): default 80 · title 20 · section 12 · two-column 110 · image 30 · quote 60 · blank 400. One idea per slide; detail goes in notes. - Body is markdown by default (headings, lists, images `![[path]]` or `![alt](url)`, code, tables). `` between blocks reveals them one at a time; `` splits a `two-column` slide. - A body that starts with `` / `` is rendered as a full document (its own styles and scripts, sandboxed). With `html: true` a fragment is inlined into the slide, style-isolated from other slides. - Speaker notes: a trailing `` comment on the slide. Write them — presenter view and the PPTX export show them. - The design box is fixed (default 1280×720) and scaled to fit everywhere; design for that box, never for a window size. - Max 300 slides. Paths are workspace-relative, no leading `/`. - Free-form authoring: `write` / `edit` the file. Structural changes by slide: `slides_edit` (insert / update / delete / move / set_deck, by number, `#id` or `$ref`). Validate with `slides_check` before calling a deck done.

path.description: Workspace-relative path ending in .slides, e.g. decks/q3-review.slides

layout.description: default | title | section | two-column | image | quote | blank

background.description: CSS color, or an image path/URL

html.description: content is raw HTML (a fragment); omit for markdown or a full HTML document

src.description: Render this workspace file as the slide (.html artboard, .md, image). No content then.

skip.description: Do not count in slide numbers

content.description: Markdown (default), raw HTML (html: true) or a full <!doctype html> document. Use <!-- step --> between blocks for incremental reveals, <!-- column --> for two-column.

overwrite.description: Replace the file if it already exists (default: FILE_EXISTS error)

tools.name: slides_edit

Idempotent inserts: an `id` that already exists is skipped with a warning. Pass `ifHash` (from a previous result) to fail with HASH_MISMATCH instead of overwriting someone else's change. Returns a compact slide map and the new contentHash. Use `edit` for small text changes inside one slide; use this to add, reorder, remove or rewrite whole slides. Word budgets per layout (body, advisory): default 80 · title 20 · section 12 · two-column 110 · image 30 · quote 60 · blank 400. One idea per slide; detail goes in notes. - Body is markdown by default (headings, lists, images `![[path]]` or `![alt](url)`, code, tables). `` between blocks reveals them one at a time; `` splits a `two-column` slide. - A body that starts with `` / `` is rendered as a full document (its own styles and scripts, sandboxed). With `html: true` a fragment is inlined into the slide, style-isolated from other slides. - Speaker notes: a trailing `` comment on the slide. Write them — presenter view and the PPTX export show them. - The design box is fixed (default 1280×720) and scaled to fit everywhere; design for that box, never for a window size. - Max 300 slides. ref.description: Name this slide so later ops can refer to it as $name

after.description: Insert right after this slide (alternative to at)

layout.description: default | title | section | two-column | image | quote | blank

background.description: CSS color, or an image path/URL

html.description: content is raw HTML (a fragment); omit for markdown or a full HTML document

src.description: Render this workspace file as the slide (.html artboard, .md, image). No content then.

skip.description: Do not count in slide numbers

content.description: Markdown (default), raw HTML (html: true) or a full <!doctype html> document. Use <!-- step --> between blocks for incremental reveals, <!-- column --> for two-column.

slide.description: A 1-based slide number, "#id" (frontmatter id), or "$n" / "$name" for a slide inserted earlier in this batch

notes.description: Replaces the notes; null removes them

frontmatter.description: Merged into the slide's frontmatter; a null value deletes that key

items.description: A 1-based slide number, "#id" (frontmatter id), or "$n" / "$name" for a slide inserted earlier in this batch

slide.description: A 1-based slide number, "#id" (frontmatter id), or "$n" / "$name" for a slide inserted earlier in this batch

ifHash.description: Content hash from a previous read/tool result; the edit fails with HASH_MISMATCH if the file changed since

tools.name: slides_check
tools.description: Check a .slides deck before calling it done: parse problems, unknown frontmatter keys, slides whose `src:` / image references are missing (SRC_MISSING — renders as a hole), moved (SRC_STALE — repairable) or unusable (SRC_UNSUPPORTED), plus advisory notes: empty slides, slides without speaker notes (NO_NOTES), bodies over the layout's word budget (TOO_MANY_WORDS). `ok: false` means at least one slide would render as a hole. Pass `repair: true` to rewrite stale paths to where the files are now (needs files:write). Read-only otherwise.

path.description: Workspace-relative path ending in .slides, e.g. decks/q3-review.slides

repair.description: Rewrite stale src/background/image paths to where the files are now (needs files:write)

tools.name: slides_export
tools.description: Export a .slides deck as a file in the workspace: `html` = one self-contained document (same renderer as the editor; open it anywhere, share it with create_share_link) or `pptx` = an editable PowerPoint built from the markdown structure (native text boxes, speaker notes attached; HTML and artboard slides export as titled text placeholders — read `warnings`). Output defaults to the deck's path with the export extension; fails with FILE_EXISTS unless overwrite: true. PDF is not produced server-side: humans print the deck from the editor (Export → Print / PDF).

path.description: Workspace-relative path ending in .slides, e.g. decks/q3-review.slides

format.description: html = one self-contained .html file; pptx = editable PowerPoint built from the markdown structure

output.description: Workspace-relative output path (default: next to the deck, same name with the export extension)

overwrite.description: Replace the output file if it exists (default: FILE_EXISTS error)

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: Search files by meaning using AI embeddings (semantic search). Use this for finding content by concept or topic rather than exact words. Best for queries like 'notes about authentication', 'ideas for the homepage', or 'what did I write about project planning'.

query.description: Natural language query describing what you're looking for

namespace.description: Where to search: 'user' (your files), 'community' (public files), or 'both'

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10)

tools.name: get_key_info
tools.description: Get information about the current API key's access level. Returns the workspace (personal or organization), folder scope (if restricted to a specific folder), and available permissions. Use this to understand what operations you can perform.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: List a file's version history (newest first): automatic before-images from agent edits, user-edit versions, named checkpoints, and revert snapshots — each with its changeset context. Use before revert_file or read_version to find the right versionId.

limit.description: Max versions to return (newest first, 1-50 — out-of-range values are clamped). Default: 20

tools.name: read_version
tools.description: Read the content of a PREVIOUS version of a file (versionId from list_versions). Use to compare old and current content — never reconstruct old content from memory.

tools.name: revert_file
tools.description: Restore a file to a previous version (versionId from list_versions). The current content is saved as a new version first, so a revert is itself undoable. For undoing a whole multi-file run, use revert_changeset.

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description: Create a named snapshot of a file's (or folder subtree's) CURRENT content. Checkpoints never get auto-pruned and can be restored later. Use BEFORE large or risky changes. Caps: 10 checkpoints per file, 200 files per folder checkpoint.

path.description: File or folder to snapshot, from the workspace root "/" (e.g. '/dogsit' or '/dogsit/README.md'). Use "/" to snapshot the whole workspace.

tools.name: list_changesets
tools.description: List recent changesets — grouped file changes from agent runs, API calls, checkpoints and reverts, newest first, with summaries and files. Use to find the changesetId for revert_changeset (e.g. when asked to undo a previous run).

limit.description: Max changesets (newest first, 1-50 — out-of-range values are clamped). Default: 10

path.description: Only changesets touching this file path

tools.name: revert_changeset
tools.description: Undo an entire changeset: restores every file's pre-change content and DELETES files the changeset created. Fails with CONFLICT when files were modified afterwards — retry with force: true to override (current states are saved as versions first, so the revert is itself undoable). For a single file use revert_file.

force.description: Revert even if files were modified after the changeset (their current state is versioned first)

instructions: Monofile: the agentic filesystem. 44 tools, proxied to https://www.monofile.ai/api/tools with your API key. Paths are workspace-absolute (/Projects/notes.md). `bash` runs read-only chains instantly and everything else (pipes, sed/awk/jq, git, python3, node) in a per-workspace sandbox whose file effects are written back, versioned. Results are JSON; `{error:{code,message}}` means the call failed (INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE → the key lacks a scope).
